channel.title: Sales on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Sales on Best of AI

item.title: lemlist
item.description:
lemlist helps sales teams and agencies reach prospects at scale. Users build sequences that combine email, LinkedIn steps, and phone tasks, and personalize messages with variables such as name and company. The brand made its name with personalized images and videos that change for each recipient, a way to stand out in crowded inboxes.

Deliverability is a major part of the product. Inbox warm-up gradually builds sender reputation, and tools check domains and monitor placement so emails land in primary inboxes, not spam. A lead database lets users find contacts and verify emails, and AI helps write openers and suggest follow-ups.

item.title: Microsoft Dynamics 365
item.description:
Dynamics 365 combines CRM and ERP in a modular set of cloud applications. The sales and customer service apps manage leads, opportunities, cases, and customer communications, while finance, supply chain, and Business Central handle accounting, inventory, purchasing, and operations. Because the modules share a data platform, a company can start with one and add others over time, and they connect closely with Microsoft 365, Teams, and Power BI.

Copilot is built throughout. In sales, it summarizes accounts and meetings, drafts emails, and suggests next steps. In service, it helps agents find answers and summarize cases, and in finance and supply chain, it supports tasks like reconciliations, collections, and spotting disruptions. AI agents take on routine tasks, such as qualifying leads or processing orders, and Copilot Studio lets companies build their own.

item.title: Mindtickle
item.description:
Mindtickle is a sales readiness platform. New hires follow structured learning paths with lessons and quizzes, and practice pitches by recording videos or role-playing with AI, receiving feedback. Managers review the practice and see how reps compare on skills.

The platform links training to results. It tracks which skills correlate with success, identifies gaps across a team, and connects with CRM data to see how readiness affects performance. AI features generate content, score practice sessions, and recommend coaching.

item.title: Smartlead
item.description:
Smartlead is built for outbound email at scale. Users connect many mailboxes, and the platform spreads sends across them, adjusts volume, and warms up new accounts so messages reach inboxes. Sequences, follow-ups, and reply management handle campaign logic.

Agencies value its multi-client workspaces, unified inbox, and analytics. AI helps personalize openers and classify replies. Integrations connect with lead databases and CRMs.

Smartlead is paid, with plans by active leads and emails. Cold email is regulated, and sending at scale damages domains if done badly. Alternatives include Instantly, lemlist, Apollo, Reply.io, and Woodpecker. Smartlead suits agencies and outbound teams.

item.title: UnleashX
item.description:
UnleashX provides voice and workflow automation. Teams configure AI agents that handle phone conversations and carry out actions across systems, such as calling leads, qualifying them, updating records, and sending follow-ups. Rules define what the worker may do.

The platform presents these as digital employees for roles like sales development and support. Outbound calling needs consent and compliance with telemarketing rules, and AI voice agents should disclose themselves.

UnleashX is paid, and independent information is limited, so run a pilot first. Alternatives include Bland AI, Retell AI, Vapi, Synthflow, and 11x. UnleashX suits small teams automating calls and follow-ups.

item.title: Conduyt
item.description:
Conduyt takes an approach to CRM pricing that departs from the per-seat model. A team pays a single price no matter how many people use the product, which suits small sales teams and agencies that would otherwise pay for every added user.

The basics are familiar: a contact database, deal pipelines, and activity tracking, with AI features that draft follow-up messages, summarize interactions, and reduce routine data entry. Positioned as AI-native, it aims to have the software do the admin work that salespeople dislike.

item.title: Encore AI
item.description:
Encore AI builds on conversation data. It analyzes recordings of calls and chats to learn which behaviors lead to good outcomes, such as how top reps handle objections or open a conversation. Those patterns become the basis for AI agents that talk with customers.

The agents can take calls or messages themselves or support human reps with live guidance. The idea is to scale the best performers’ approach across a team instead of relying on training alone. Companies with large volumes of calls and recorded history are the target.

item.title: Amplemarket
item.description:
Amplemarket helps sales teams find and contact potential customers. It combines a database of B2B contacts and companies with search filters and intent signals, so reps can build lists of people who match their ideal customer and show signs of interest, such as hiring, funding, or website activity. Contact data is verified and enriched to reduce bounced emails and wrong numbers.

Outreach happens through multichannel sequences that mix email, phone calls, and social steps such as LinkedIn messages. A parallel dialer lets reps call through lists quickly. The AI layer researches each account and prospect, drafts personalized emails and call notes, and surfaces the best people to contact first. Duo Intelligence is Amplemarket’s approach of AI preparing the work while the rep reviews and sends, instead of fully automatic sending.

item.title: Cognism
item.description:
Cognism helps salespeople reach the right people. Its database covers companies and contacts across regions, with a reputation for strong coverage in Europe and for verified mobile numbers, which are valuable for cold calling. Users filter by role, industry, size, and technology, then export or sync contacts to their CRM.

Intent data adds timing. Signals show which accounts are researching topics related to a product, so teams can prioritize outreach. Compliance is a selling point: the company screens contacts against do-not-call lists and says it follows privacy rules like GDPR, which matters for outreach in Europe.

item.title: Gainsight
item.description:
Gainsight was one of the first platforms for the customer success discipline. It pulls usage, support, survey, and billing data to produce a health score for every customer, so teams can see who needs attention before a renewal is at risk. Playbooks guide the steps a manager should take for each situation.

AI features predict churn, suggest next actions, summarize account history, and draft communications. Surveys, in-app engagement, and a community product complete the suite, and the company has expanded into customer education. Reports help leaders show the effect of customer success on retention.

item.title: Highspot
item.description:
Highspot helps sales organizations make sure reps find and use the right material. Marketing publishes decks, case studies, and playbooks in one library, reps search or get recommendations based on the deal stage and customer, and managers see which assets are used and which correlate with wins.

Training and coaching tools are part of the platform, including practice exercises, call reviews, and guided selling plays. AI features recommend content, summarize accounts, and generate tailored messages and presentations. Integrations with CRMs and communication tools bring this into reps’ daily workflow.

item.title: Kaspr
item.description:
Kaspr is a contact data tool for outbound sales. While browsing a LinkedIn profile, a user clicks the Kaspr extension to reveal a professional email address and phone number, then saves the contact to a CRM or a list. It also supports bulk searches and enrichment of existing records.

The company emphasizes European data and compliance with privacy rules like GDPR, and offers ways for individuals to opt out of the database. Credits limit how many contact details a user can reveal each month, and integrations connect with CRMs and sales engagement tools.

item.title: Lusha
item.description:
Lusha helps sales and recruiting teams get in touch with prospects. While viewing a profile on LinkedIn or a company website, a user clicks the Lusha extension to reveal contact information, then saves it to a CRM. A database search finds contacts by role, company size, and industry.

Additional features include intent signals, technology data, and enrichment of existing lists, as well as integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, and sales engagement tools. The company emphasizes compliance with privacy laws and offers ways for people to opt out.

item.title: Seamless AI
item.description:
Seamless.AI helps salespeople find who to contact. Users search by title, industry, and location, or use a browser extension to look up contacts on websites, and the platform returns emails and phone numbers pulled from public sources and its database. Lists export to CRMs and engagement tools.

Real-time search and enrichment aim to keep data fresh, and intent signals show which accounts may be in a buying cycle. AI features help write outreach and prioritize accounts.

item.title: Seismic
item.description:
Seismic organizes marketing and sales content so reps can find and use it. Instead of searching shared drives, a seller gets recommended decks, case studies, and playbooks based on the deal stage and customer, and can assemble personalized presentations quickly.

Analytics show which content gets used and which correlates with wins, and engagement data tells sellers how buyers interact with shared materials. Coaching and training modules, and AI that writes tailored messages and summaries, add to the suite.

item.title: Showpad
item.description:
Showpad helps sellers find and use approved content. Marketing publishes decks, videos, and guides, and reps get recommendations based on the customer and deal stage. Buyers receive shared links that track engagement, which tells sellers what resonated.

Coaching and training are the other half. Reps practice pitches and receive AI feedback, learning paths build skills, and managers see progress. The platform integrates with CRMs and works well in industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, and technology.

item.title: Catchlight
item.description:
Catchlight is a lead scoring tool for financial advisory firms. It enriches a prospect’s profile with data such as estimated income, investable assets, age range, and interests, then applies a model trained on past conversions to produce a score showing how likely they are to become a client.

Advisors use it to prioritize their time. Instead of calling every inquiry, they can focus on those with the best fit, and see context to start a conversation. It integrates with CRMs used by advisors, such as Wealthbox, and appears in platforms that serve wealth management firms.

item.title: Apollo
item.description:
Apollo gives sales teams a place to find and contact prospects. Users search a database of people and companies by title, industry, size, and technology used, then add leads to email sequences, calling lists, and LinkedIn tasks. A browser extension finds contact details as you browse the web.

The platform includes tools for the whole outbound workflow: email verification, scheduling, a dialer, meeting booking, analytics, and integrations with CRMs like Salesforce and HubSpot. AI features help write messages, score leads, and automate steps, and workflows can enrich existing records to keep a CRM current.

item.title: Apollo
item.description: Apollo is one of the most used tools for outbound sales. At its core is a searchable database of business contacts and companies, which you can filter by job title, industry, company size, location, technology used, and more. You export the matches or push them into sequences, and Apollo supplies emails and phone numbers. Startups and small sales teams like that it bundles data and outreach in one affordable product.

item.title: Chorus.ai
item.description:
Chorus records sales calls and video meetings and turns them into searchable transcripts. Managers can look through conversations to see what customers say about price, competitors, or objections, instead of relying on reps’ summaries. The tool tags topics, tracks talk time and question patterns, and highlights key moments, which makes it faster to review a call than to listen to the whole recording.

The AI layer analyzes patterns across many conversations. It can surface deals that appear to be at risk, detect competitor mentions, summarize each call, and suggest next steps. Coaching features let managers share clips, give feedback, and compare reps against top performers. Integrations with Salesforce and other CRMs send call data and notes into the customer record so reps spend less time on updates.

item.title: Clari
item.description:
Clari began as a tool to make sales forecasting more reliable. It reads CRM data and signals from email, calendar, and calls to show how deals are progressing, then rolls those into a forecast that managers can inspect by team, region, and stage. The goal is to replace spreadsheet-based forecast calls with data that people trust.

AI helps spot trouble. It scores deals, flags those with stalled activity or missing stakeholders, and suggests actions. Conversation intelligence summarizes calls and highlights risks, and pipeline inspection tools show where coverage is thin. Revenue leaders use it to prepare for board and forecast meetings.

item.title: Conversica
item.description:
Conversica automates the follow-up that sales teams often drop. When a lead comes in, the AI assistant sends personalized messages, reads replies, answers questions, and tries to book a meeting. If a prospect does not respond, it continues with a sequence of nudges, which keeps leads from going cold.

The assistants are used in industries such as automotive, education, software, and financial services, where large volumes of inquiries arrive. Conversation data flows into the CRM, so salespeople see which leads are qualified and what was said. The company has added generative AI to make conversations more natural.

item.title: Gong
item.description:
Gong captures sales conversations and turns them into insight. It records calls and meetings, transcribes them, and pulls in emails and CRM data, then analyzes what is happening across the pipeline: which topics come up in deals that close, how often competitors are mentioned, how much reps talk compared with customers, and where deals are stalling. Managers can search a library of calls instead of relying on reps’ summaries.

The AI features save time at several levels. Calls are summarized with key points and next steps, which are written back to the CRM. Deal boards highlight risks, such as no recent contact with a decision-maker, and forecasting tools estimate which deals will close. Coaching tools find moments to review and compare behavior across reps, and newer AI agents help with tasks such as preparing for meetings, researching accounts, and drafting follow-ups.

item.title: HubSpot CRM
item.description: HubSpot CRM is the shared database underneath every HubSpot product, and it can also be used on its own at no cost. It stores contacts, companies, deals, and tickets, logs emails and calls against each record, and shows a pipeline of deals by stage. Connecting Gmail or Outlook means sent and received messages are attached to the right contact automatically, so people spend less time on manual data entry. For a small business that has been running on spreadsheets, it is an easy first step into a real CRM.

item.title: Hunter
item.description: Hunter is a tool for finding contact details for business outreach. A Domain Search shows the email addresses associated with a company along with the sources where they were found, and the email pattern the company uses. An Email Finder takes a person’s name and company and returns the most likely address with a confidence score. Email Verifier checks whether an address is valid and likely to deliver, which reduces bounces.

item.title: LinkedIn Sales Navigator
item.description:
Sales Navigator gives salespeople deeper access to LinkedIn’s network. It provides advanced filters for finding people and companies, such as by seniority, function, company size, industry, and recent job changes. Users save leads and accounts into lists, and the system sends alerts when something relevant happens, like a prospect changing jobs or a company hiring in a certain department, which can prompt a timely message.

Further features support outreach. InMail messages reach people outside your network, TeamLink shows how colleagues are connected to a prospect for warm introductions, and integrations sync with CRMs such as Salesforce and HubSpot to keep records current. AI tools recommend leads, summarize accounts, and suggest ways to start a conversation, using the profile and activity data on the platform.

item.title: Outreach
item.description:
Outreach is used by sales teams to run structured prospecting and follow-up at scale. Reps enroll leads in sequences that combine emails, calls, LinkedIn steps, and tasks, and the platform schedules each step, tracks replies, and logs activity to the CRM. Managers can see which messages and cadences perform best, and automated rules route leads and keep work organized.

Over time, Outreach has added revenue intelligence and AI. Conversation intelligence records and analyzes calls, deal health scoring flags risk, and forecasting tools combine activity and pipeline data to estimate outcomes. AI assistants summarize meetings, draft emails, suggest next steps, and increasingly act as agents that research accounts or manage parts of the pipeline.

item.title: People.ai
item.description:
People.ai solves the data entry problem in sales. Instead of relying on reps to log everything, it connects to email, calendars, and phone systems and records contacts, meetings, and conversations, then matches them to the right accounts and opportunities in the CRM. That keeps records current and gives managers a more complete picture of how engaged each deal is.

On top of the data, it provides analytics and AI. Dashboards show activity, engagement with key contacts, and whether deals are at risk, and forecasting tools estimate which will close. AI agents can summarize accounts, answer questions about the pipeline in natural language, and prepare reps for meetings. The aim is to give sales leaders a reliable view without chasing updates.

item.title: Pipedrive
item.description: Pipedrive is designed by and for salespeople, with the pipeline at the center. Deals appear as cards that move across stages, from first contact to closed, so reps can see at a glance what needs attention. Each deal has activities, emails, notes, and files attached, and the system reminds you of follow-ups so nothing slips. Compared with big CRM suites, the interface is clean and quick to learn, which suits small and growing sales teams.

item.title: Salesforce
item.description: Salesforce is the CRM that large companies tend to run their sales and customer operations on. It tracks leads, accounts, opportunities, and support cases, and it is sold as separate clouds for Sales, Service, Marketing, and Commerce, with Slack, Tableau, and MuleSoft added for collaboration, analytics, and integration. Underneath is a platform that lets companies build custom objects, workflows, and apps, which is why Salesforce setups can look very different from one company to the next.

item.title: SalesLoft
item.description:
Salesloft helps sales teams organize outbound and follow-up work. Reps follow cadences, which are structured sequences of emails, calls, and social touches, and the platform tells them who to contact next and records each activity in the CRM. Managers can see which messages and sequences generate replies and meetings, and coach reps with call recordings and analytics.

The platform has expanded into revenue orchestration. Conversation intelligence records and summarizes calls, deal management tracks stage progress and risk, and forecasting tools combine pipeline data with engagement signals. Salesloft acquired Drift for conversational marketing and has combined with Clari, a revenue forecasting company, to build a broader revenue platform. AI assistants prepare meeting briefs, draft messages, and suggest next steps.

item.title: Zoho CRM
item.description:
Zoho CRM covers the normal work of sales: tracking leads and contacts, managing deals through a pipeline, logging calls and emails, and forecasting revenue. It supports multiple channels, including phone, email, live chat, and social media, and lets you build custom modules and fields so it can reflect how a business actually sells. Workflow rules, assignment rules, and blueprints enforce a consistent sales process without manual follow-up.

Zia is the AI layer. It scores leads by how likely they are to convert, predicts which deals will close, spots unusual activity, and recommends the best time to contact a prospect. It can answer questions in plain language, summarize records, and help draft emails. Because Zoho builds its own models, it positions this as a cost-effective alternative to enterprise AI add-ons. Integrations connect with Zoho’s other products such as Campaigns, Books, and Desk, and with outside tools through a marketplace.

item.title: ZoomInfo
item.description:
ZoomInfo provides one of the largest databases of business contacts and companies. Sales and marketing teams search by title, industry, company size, location, and technology to build lists, and see verified email addresses, direct phone numbers, org charts, and firmographic details. Intent data shows which companies are researching topics related to a product, helping teams reach out when interest is high.

The platform has expanded from data into a workflow product. It includes tools for sales engagement, marketing advertising, conversation intelligence through Chorus, and enrichment that keeps CRM records up to date automatically. AI features include assistants that research accounts, draft outreach, and recommend who to contact, and agents that handle prospecting tasks. It integrates with Salesforce, HubSpot, and other systems.

item.title: Attio
item.description:
Attio starts from the idea that every company sells differently. Instead of fixed objects like leads and opportunities, teams build their own structures, such as customers, partners, or investors, and link them. The interface feels more like a spreadsheet and a database than a traditional CRM, so it is easier to reshape.

Data fills in with little typing. Attio connects to email and calendar to log interactions, enriches company and contact details, and shows the strength of relationships. AI features summarize accounts, answer questions about the pipeline, and fill in fields from conversations. Workflow automation moves records, sends notifications, and updates data.

item.title: Close
item.description:
Close takes the position that sales reps should do their work from one screen. Calls, emails, and texts happen inside the CRM and are logged automatically, so there is less manual data entry and a complete history on each lead. Power dialers let reps work through lists quickly.

Sequences automate multi-step outreach that mixes email, calls, and texts, and workflows keep pipelines moving. AI features transcribe and summarize calls, suggest follow-ups, and score leads, which helps managers coach and helps reps decide where to spend time. Reporting shows activity and results by rep.

item.title: Copper
item.description:
Copper integrates with the tools its users already work in. Because it lives inside Gmail and connects with Google Calendar, Drive, and Docs, contacts and conversations are logged automatically, so reps do not have to copy information into a separate system.

The CRM covers the usual sales functions: contacts, companies, deals, pipelines, tasks, and reporting. Project management features track work after a deal closes, which suits agencies and service firms. AI features help summarize communication and suggest follow-ups, and workflow automation moves deals through stages.

item.title: Folk
item.description:
Folk is a relationship manager for people who find traditional CRMs heavy. Users import contacts from email, LinkedIn, and spreadsheets, organize them into groups, and track conversations and deals in a clean interface. It suits agencies, recruiters, investors, and founders who manage many relationships.

AI and automation reduce the manual work. Enrichment fills in details like company and role, a browser extension saves profiles from LinkedIn, and sequences send personalized emails at scale. AI helps write messages and summarize history, and reminders prompt follow-ups so nobody falls through the cracks.

item.title: Freshsales
item.description:
Freshsales is a sales CRM that keeps lead and deal information in one view. Teams track contacts, run pipelines, and log calls and emails, with a built-in phone and chat so reps can contact prospects without switching tools. Automation moves leads through stages and assigns tasks.

Freddy AI assists with prioritization. It scores leads by likelihood to convert, predicts which deals will close, and suggests next best actions, while generative features draft emails and summarize conversations. Analytics show pipeline health, and integrations connect with Freshdesk, marketing tools, and common business apps.

item.title: Jiminny
item.description:
Jiminny captures conversations between sales teams and customers. It records calls and meetings, creates transcripts, and uses AI to summarize them, extract action items, and detect topics, objections, and talk ratios. Managers use this to coach reps with specific examples.

Deal insights help forecast. The platform flags risks such as lack of next steps or missing stakeholders, and keeps the CRM updated with notes and fields without manual entry. Search across calls lets teams find how customers talk about competitors or pricing.

item.title: Kixie
item.description:
Kixie speeds up phone outreach. A power dialer calls through a list automatically, local presence shows numbers with the prospect’s area code to improve answer rates, and voicemail drop leaves a prerecorded message with one click. Calls and texts sync with CRMs such as HubSpot, Salesforce, and Pipedrive.

Automation sends text messages and follow-ups triggered by call outcomes, and a coaching feature lets managers listen in. AI transcribes calls, summarizes them, and gives feedback on conversations. Analytics track activity, connect rates, and results by rep.

item.title: Oliv AI
item.description:
Oliv AI assists sellers before, during, and after calls. Before a meeting, it gathers context on the account and contacts and drafts a briefing. During the call, it records and transcribes. Afterward, it writes notes, updates the CRM, and drafts follow-up emails.

For managers, it scores deals against frameworks such as MEDDIC and highlights risks and gaps, which supports coaching and forecasting. The product presents these functions as agents that take over routine sales admin.

item.title: Quantified AI
item.description:
Quantified AI helps sales reps practice before they talk to real customers. A rep enters a simulated conversation with an AI buyer that responds in real time, raises objections, and changes direction, and the system scores the performance on things like discovery, handling pushback, and messaging.

Managers use the results to see who needs coaching and track progress over time, and companies can create scenarios that mirror their own sales motions and products. Practice is available any time, which helps new hires ramp faster than relying only on role-play with colleagues.

item.title: Revenue.io
item.description:
Revenue.io, formerly RingDNA, combines calling with conversation intelligence. During a call, it listens and surfaces prompts, such as a competitor battlecard or the right answer to a pricing objection. After the call, it transcribes, summarizes, and scores conversations against a playbook.

Managers get coaching insights and forecasting signals. The platform includes a dialer and integrates with Salesforce, so call data flows into the CRM. AI assistants draft follow-ups and update records.

item.title: Salesflare
item.description:
Salesflare fills itself in. It connects to email, calendar, and phone, then builds contact and company profiles with conversation history, social data, and notes, so sales reps do not need to type everything. A timeline shows every interaction with a contact.

Features include pipelines, workflows, email tracking, and sequences, plus an intelligent assistant that nudges reps when a lead has gone quiet. It works with Gmail, Outlook, and a mobile app.

item.title: Streak
item.description:
Streak adds pipeline management to Gmail. Users create boxes for deals, candidates, or projects, move them through stages, and see all related emails, notes, and files in one place. Because it sits in the inbox, there is little context switching.

Features include mail merge, email tracking, scheduling, shared inboxes, and automations. AI helps summarize threads and draft emails. It suits small teams that already run on Google Workspace.

Streak has a free plan and paid tiers. It is tied to Gmail. Alternatives include Copper, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Close, and Attio. Streak suits small teams working from the inbox.

item.title: Clay
item.description:
Clay works like a spreadsheet for sales and marketing data. You start with a list of companies or people, and Clay adds columns that look up information, such as emails, job titles, funding, technologies used, and recent news, pulling from many data providers. Its waterfall enrichment tries one source after another until it finds a result, which improves coverage over relying on a single vendor.

The AI part is a web research agent that can visit sites and answer questions you define for each row, for example whether a company has a mobile app or what it sells. Results feed into AI-written emails and messages tailored to each prospect, and workflows push the finished leads into CRMs and outreach tools like HubSpot, Salesforce, Smartlead, or Outreach. Growth teams use it to build very specific lists and trigger outreach when signals appear.

item.title: Cora Intelligence
item.description:
Cora is meant to stand in for a junior sales development rep. A founder describes the ideal customer, and the tool searches for matching prospects, researches them, and writes personalized messages. The goal is to generate conversations without a dedicated hire.

This kind of tool appeals to small companies that need pipeline but lack the budget or time for a sales team. Results depend on how clearly the target customer is defined and how good the messaging is. Automated outreach also has to comply with email rules and can harm a sender’s reputation if poorly targeted.

item.title: Instantly
item.description:
Instantly is built for outbound email at scale. You connect as many sending accounts as you like, and the platform rotates them to spread volume, which helps keep each account within safe sending limits. An automated warm-up network exchanges emails between accounts to build sender reputation, and tools check deliverability so campaigns are more likely to reach the inbox. Sequences handle follow-ups and stop when someone replies.

AI and data features add to the core sender. A lead database lets users find prospects by role, industry, and location, AI helps write and personalize email copy, and a unified inbox collects replies from all accounts in one place. Analytics show opens, replies, and bounces, and integrations connect with CRMs and automation tools. Agencies, sales teams, and lead generation businesses are the main users.

item.title: Intuo
item.description:
Intuo helps salespeople prepare. It tracks news and events about accounts, markets, and competitors, filters what matters to the user’s deals, and delivers a short brief with suggested conversation starters. The goal is to replace time spent searching the web before each call.

Account executives and sales leaders use it to stay informed about prospects and to find reasons to reach out. The briefs adapt to the seller’s focus areas, and some features suggest actions or talking points tied to the signals.

item.title: Jason AI
item.description:
Jason AI acts as an automated sales development rep within Reply.io. It finds prospects, writes personalized emails and LinkedIn messages, sends them, and replies to responses to move conversations toward a meeting. It works within Reply.io’s sequencing system, which also handles calls and tasks.

Users give it information about their product and target customers, and Jason builds campaigns. A human can review messages and take over when a lead is interested. The goal is to let small teams reach more prospects without hiring more reps.

item.title: Lavender
item.description:
Lavender sits in your email composer and gives feedback in real time. As you write a cold email, it gives a score and highlights problems: sentences that are too long, language that sounds salesy, a missing clear ask, or a message that is too focused on you instead of the recipient. It suggests edits and shows how changes affect the score, acting like a coach looking over your shoulder.

Personalization is a second pillar. Lavender can pull in information about the recipient, such as their role, company news, and social posts, and suggest personalized opening lines and talking points. A Chrome extension works in Gmail and Outlook and integrates with sales engagement tools, so it fits existing workflows. Managers can see team-wide analytics and coach reps on writing.

item.title: Lightfield
item.description:
Lightfield rethinks the CRM as a system that fills itself. It connects to email, calendar, and call recordings, and extracts contacts, companies, deals, and notes automatically, so records stay current without reps typing. The aim is to remove the data entry that makes CRMs unpopular.

Beyond capturing data, it uses the context to help with work, such as drafting follow-ups, answering questions about accounts, and surfacing deals that need attention. The team behind it previously built Tome, a presentation tool, before turning to this product.
